nodes.label: Vieta's Formulas
nodes.applicable_when: When the problem involves roots of a polynomial and asks for symmetric expressions (sums, products, power sums) of the roots.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Identify the polynomial and its roots. 2. Express the target via elementary symmetric polynomials (e1=sum roots, e2=sum of pairs, en=product). 3. Use Newton's identities if power sums are needed.

nodes.label: Substitution & Variable Elimination
nodes.applicable_when: When the problem has multiple variables with symmetric or structured constraints, or when a substitution simplifies a functional equation or system.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Identify the dominant constraint or symmetry. 2. Let a new variable represent a key expression. 3. Rewrite all conditions in terms of the new variable. 4. Solve the reduced problem and back-substitute.

nodes.label: Generating Functions
nodes.applicable_when: When the problem involves counting sequences with linear recurrences, partitions, or convolutions.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Set up G(x) = sum a_n x^n. 2. Translate the recurrence/constraint into an algebraic equation for G(x). 3. Solve via partial fractions or known identities. 4. Extract the target coefficient.

nodes.label: Chinese Remainder Theorem
nodes.applicable_when: When the problem asks for a number satisfying multiple modular congruences with pairwise coprime moduli.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Verify moduli are pairwise coprime. 2. Compute M = product of all moduli. 3. For each congruence x ≡ a_i (mod m_i), compute M_i=M/m_i and its inverse mod m_i. 4. Sum a_i*M_i*(M_i^{-1} mod m_i) and reduce mod M.

nodes.label: Fermat's Little Theorem & Euler's Theorem
nodes.applicable_when: When computing large modular powers or inverses, or when the exponent is much larger than the modulus.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. For prime p and gcd(a,p)=1: a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p); reduce exponent mod (p-1). 2. For general n: a^phi(n) ≡ 1 (mod n) when gcd(a,n)=1. 3. Use Python pow(base, exp, mod) for fast computation.

nodes.label: AM-GM & Cauchy-Schwarz Inequalities
nodes.applicable_when: When optimizing a sum/product subject to constraints, or when proving an inequality involving positive reals.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. AM-GM: (a1+...+an)/n >= (a1*...*an)^(1/n); equality when all a_i equal. 2. Cauchy-Schwarz: (sum a_i*b_i)^2 <= (sum a_i^2)*(sum b_i^2). 3. Identify the equality condition to pinpoint the extremum.

nodes.label: Inclusion-Exclusion Principle
nodes.applicable_when: When counting elements satisfying at least one of several properties, especially when direct counting overcounts.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Define sets A_1,...,A_k of 'bad' elements. 2. Apply |A_1∪...∪A_k| = sum|A_i| - sum|A_i∩A_j| + ... 3. Subtract from total to get the count of 'good' elements.

nodes.label: Bijection, Symmetry & Double Counting
nodes.applicable_when: When two combinatorial quantities seem different but are actually equal, or when the problem has exploitable symmetry.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Identify a bijection between two sets or a symmetry operation. 2. Double-count: count the same quantity in two ways and equate. 3. Use the bijection to simplify the count.

nodes.label: Recurrence Relations & Dynamic Programming
nodes.applicable_when: When the problem can be broken into overlapping subproblems, or when a sequence is defined recursively.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Identify base cases and the recurrence f(n) = expr(f(n-1), f(n-2), ...). 2. Compute iteratively (bottom-up DP) or cache (memoization). 3. Check for closed-form solution via characteristic equation.

nodes.label: Stars & Bars / Combinatorial Identities
nodes.applicable_when: When distributing identical items into distinct bins, or computing combinations with repetition.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Non-negative solutions to x1+...+xk=n: C(n+k-1, k-1). 2. Positive solutions: substitute yi=xi-1. 3. Apply Vandermonde or other identities to simplify final sums.

nodes.label: Power of a Point & Circle Theorems
nodes.applicable_when: When the problem involves a point and a circle with intersecting or tangent lines, chord-chord or secant-secant configurations.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Power of point P = PA*PB for any chord through P. 2. External: (segment)*(whole secant) = (tangent)^2. 3. Use inscribed angle theorem and extended law of sines for angle relations.

nodes.label: Coordinate System & Analytic Geometry
nodes.applicable_when: When geometric objects have natural algebraic descriptions, or when pure synthetic approaches seem intractable.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Place the figure in coordinates (choose origin/axes to minimize complexity). 2. Express all constraints as equations. 3. Solve algebraically. 4. Compute the geometric quantity (distance, area, angle) analytically.

nodes.label: Conditional Probability & Bayes' Theorem
nodes.applicable_when: When the problem conditions on an event, asks for P(A|B), or when information is revealed sequentially.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Identify P(A), P(B|A), P(B|A^c). 2. Apply Bayes: P(A|B) = P(B|A)*P(A) / P(B). 3. Enumerate states if the state space is small; use law of total probability otherwise.

nodes.label: Expected Value & Linearity of Expectation
nodes.applicable_when: When the problem asks for an expected count of events, especially when events are not independent.
nodes.actionable_steps: 1. Define indicator random variables X_i = 1 if event i occurs. 2. E[X] = sum P(X_i=1) by linearity of expectation. 3. For Markov chains: set up E[T|state] equations and solve.
